title: Finite coproducts and sifted colimits imply coherent cocompleteness
statement: Use quasicategories, spaces, coherent diagrams and colimits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the fixed nested universes and smallness convention of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Let $\mathcal E$ be an infinity category in the larger universe. A small infinity category $I$ is sifted if the colimit functor $\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal S)\to\mathcal S$ on small spaces preserves finite products, including the empty product. If $\mathcal E$ admits all small sifted colimits and all finite coproducts, including an initial object, then $\mathcal E$ admits colimits of every small simplicial diagram. No local smallness, accessibility or monadicity of $\mathcal E$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.8.15 and Remark 5.5.8.16, cases (2) and (3); the cocompleteness input in Gepner–Haugseng, Lemma A.5.8, printed p.710. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Let $K$ be an arbitrary small simplicial set and $F:K\to\mathcal E$ an arbitrary coherent diagram. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-finite-coproduct-envelope] to obtain a small quasicategory $J$, a map $i:K\to J$, a finite-coproduct-preserving $\widehat F:J\to\mathcal E$, and $\eta:F\simeq\widehat F i$, with the displayed left Kan mapping-space equivalence against every $H:J\to\mathcal E$. The hypothesis needed on $\mathcal E$ is only its given finite coproducts. In particular we have not used local smallness to build a full subcategory of $\mathcal E$: the envelope $J$ is small independently of the sizes of its image's mapping spaces.

source.place: Remark 5.3.5.9 and Proposition 5.3.6.2, finite-coproduct completion; agent application to the indexing shape.

proof.text: For $a,b\in J$, let $Q_{a,b}=((a,b)\downarrow\operatorname{diag}_J)$ be the coherent category of cospans $a\to z\leftarrow b$. This is the cocone category of the discrete two-object diagram. The coproduct cospan $q$ is initial: for any cospan $\gamma$ with apex $z$, [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{Q_{a,b}}(q,\gamma)$ with the homotopy fiber over $\gamma$ of the coproduct equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_J(a\amalg b,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_J(a,z)\times\operatorname{Map}_J(b,z)$, hence it is contractible. Apply [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to $T:\Delta^0\to Q_{a,b}$ selecting $q$, with $\mathcal D_0=Q_{a,b}$. Its hypothesis is precisely $\operatorname{Map}_{Q_{a,b}}(q,\gamma)\simeq *$. Its counit supplies a coherent transformation $\operatorname{const}_q\to\operatorname{id}_{Q_{a,b}}$, a simplicial map $Q_{a,b}\times\Delta^1\to Q_{a,b}$. Realizing its simplex prisms gives a homotopy from the constant map at $q$ to the identity, so $Q_{a,b}$ is weakly contractible. The implication (3) to (1) of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test], with $u=\operatorname{diag}_J:J\to J\times J$, proves that the diagonal is final.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.3.1; elementary coproduct-cospan calculation and contraction using the cited coherent calculus.

proof.text: The initial object of $J$ makes $J$ nonempty. By step 2 its diagonal is final, so [lem-coef-sifted-nerve-index-calculus] makes $J$ sifted in the space-valued sense, including preservation of the empty product. The assumed existence of all small sifted colimits in $\mathcal E$ therefore gives a colimiting cocone $\beta:\widehat F\to\Delta_J L$. Restrict it along $i$ and compose with $\eta$ to get the actual cocone $\alpha=(\beta i)\eta:F\to\Delta_K L$. All index data are in the smaller universe.

source.place: Definition 5.5.8.1, Lemma 5.5.8.11 and Remark 5.5.8.12; application of the given sifted-colimit hypothesis.

proof.text:
For every $x\in\mathcal E$, the cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], applied to the colimiting $\beta$, gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(L,x)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)}(\widehat F,\Delta_Jx)$, sending $a$ to $(\Delta_Ja)\beta$. Apply the full mapping-space equivalence in [lem-coef-infinity-finite-coproduct-envelope] with $H=\Delta_Jx$. Its composite with the preceding equivalence is
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(L,x)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(F,\Delta_Kx),\qquad a\longmapsto (\Delta_Ka)(\beta i)\eta=(\Delta_Ka)\alpha.$$
The equality identifies the comparison induced by our actual cocone, on whole mapping spaces and naturally in $x$, rather than only a bijection on homotopy classes. The dual cocone clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] now proves that $\alpha$ is colimiting. Since $K$ and $F$ were arbitrary, this proves every required colimit. For $K=\varnothing$ the same argument produces an initial object: the target transformation space is a point; equivalently one may use the assumed empty coproduct directly.

source.place: Section 4.3.2 (left Kan universal property), applied to constant target functors; agent two-map calculation of the cocone universal property.
